conductor_at_2.note: all odd: conductor depends on mod 8 congruences

conductor_at_5.note: 5∤xz: depends on F(x) irreducibility over Q_5

conductor.note: Serre level is an ideal in O_{Q(√5)}. Norm gives the rational level. The (5,p,3) paper computes HMFs up to norm 400.

maximal_subgroups.name: A₅ (exceptional)
maximal_subgroups.obstruction: Only for p ≡ ±1 mod 5 → 7 ≡ 2 mod 5 → EXCLUDED

p7_specific.note: A₅ subgroup excluded because 7 ≡ 2 mod 5 (not ±1). S₄ can be checked via weight considerations. Borel case (reducibility) requires direct computation. Cartan cases require checking if ρ̄₇ is dihedral.

big_image.verification_strategy:
For each conductor level 𝔫 over Q(√5):
  1. Compute ρ̄₇ from the HGM at that level
  2. Check image is not in Borel (reducibility test)
  3. Check image is not dihedral (Cartan test)
  4. S₄ check via Serre weight
  5. A₅ already excluded (7 ≡ 2 mod 5)
If all pass → Big Image holds for p=7

logic.step_1: Start with mod-7 representation ρ̄₇ from HGM ℋ⁺ or ℋ⁻
logic.step_2: Check Big Image: does im(ρ̄₇) ⊇ SL₂(F₇)?
logic.step_3_yes: Big Image holds → apply level-lowering → reach conductor 𝔫 → check S₂(Γ₀(𝔫)) = 0
logic.step_3_no: Big Image fails → switch to mod-5 or mod-3
logic.step_4_mod5: Mod-5: ρ̄₅ from ℋ⁺ specialized differently. Since 5 ramifies in Q(√5), use Fontaine-Laffaille
logic.step_4_mod3: Mod-3: ρ̄₃ reducible → use Langlands-Tunnell (as in original Wiles). Known modular.
logic.step_5: Whichever prime gives irreducible ρ̄, apply Taylor-Wiles patching to get R = T
logic.step_6: If R = T = 0 (no modular forms at that level), then no solution exists → Beal holds for (3,5,7)

switch.key_insight: The 3-5 switch for (3,5,7) is STRONGER than for FLT because we have THREE primes to switch between, not just two. If mod-7 fails, try mod-5. If mod-5 fails, try mod-3. The Langlands-Tunnell theorem guarantees mod-3 always works as a starting point (the representation is automatically modular).
switch.goldilocks_interaction: The degree-3 cyclotomic field from 7 (Q(ζ₇)⁺ = Q(cos(2π/7))) is NOT the base field in our ordering. Our base field is Q(√5) from the q=5 exponent. The 7 appears only as the mod-p prime, where it creates a finite-image obstruction — not a field extension obstruction.
